_comment: Categorised false-positive taxonomy derived from the existing blind-labelled corpus. Source of truth: benchmarks/results/random_corpus/BLIND_LABELS.json. Regenerate with the script recorded in docs/improvement/CODE_REVIEW.md. Feeds the Phase 3 annotation guidelines.

corpus_totals.note: PRECISION.json reports high_risk n=6 (tp=2, fp=4). That is the post-domain-gating PRODUCTION subset (N=115). The full labelled set (201) contains 24 high-risk false positives. Both figures are correct for their scope; conflating them would misstate either.

homonym_compute_vs_human.description: Regulated-domain term whose ordinary meaning in ML/systems code is unrelated to people. The regex is lexically correct; the sense is wrong.
homonym_compute_vs_human.requires: domain/context signal (package purpose, sibling imports, call-site semantics)

domain_word_collision.description: A safety/critical/justice keyword appears in generic engineering vocabulary (safety checker, critical section, factory).

modality_confusion.description: Audio/vision processing read as biometric identification. Speech datasets and video pipelines are not biometric identification systems.

non_production_context.description: Finding sits in tutorials, tests, notebooks, legacy or previous_versions paths that do not ship.

homonym_compute_vs_human.labeller_note: worker_process.py in fastdeploy refers to compute worker processes for model serving, not human worker monitoring or employment task allocation.

headline_conclusion: The high-risk false positives are overwhelmingly semantic, not lexical. The patterns that fire use genuine EU AI Act Annex III vocabulary (for example 'task allocation' in Annex III 4(b)); the failure is that the same words carry an unrelated ordinary meaning in ML and systems code. Tightening the regexes cannot fix this class without destroying recall on real cases. The fix space is context: package-level domain classification, co-occurrence requirements, path scoping, or an optional semantic verification tier.
